title: Replace combinational DIV/REM array with a 34-cycle serial divider; share one multiplier
motivation:
The baseline closes timing at only 5.44 MHz. The reported worst path is 199.8 ns
with 156 logic cells / ~150 logic levels, going MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit -> ex_stage
-> alu -> EX/MEM.alu_result (which Gowin absorbs into the dmem BSRAM address register).
A path that deep can only be the four combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` array dividers
in alu.sv (signed/unsigned quotient and remainder). They also explain the 12.3K LUT4
count. The three separate 64-bit multipliers (mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su) add area and
an extra operand-mux layer on top of that. Every other path in this 5-stage core
(forwarding mux -> adder -> redirect, BSRAM read -> load align) is an order of
magnitude shorter. CoreMark's timed region executes essentially no DIV/REM
(the compiler turns constant divisions into multiply-high at -O3, and the printf/
setup code that divides sits outside the start/stop MMIO markers), so an
iterative divider costs ~0 cycles of IPC while removing the dominant critical path.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Take DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU out of the combinational ALU and execute them in a small
radix-2 sequential divider that stalls the pipeline in EX for ~34 cycles. Fmax
should then be set by the single 33x33 multiplier / forwarding / adder paths
(tens of ns instead of ~200 ns), i.e. a several-fold Fmax gain at essentially
unchanged cycles-per-iteration. Concretely:

1. New rtl/divider.sv (`divider`). Inputs: clock, reset, `start` (a DIV-class op is
   in EX and EX/MEM is not dmem-stalled), `a`, `b` (post-forwarding rs1/rs2),
   `is_signed`, `want_rem`. Outputs: `busy`, `done`, `result[31:0]`, plus
   `a_q`/`b_q` (the raw latched operands, RVFI-only so synthesis prunes them from
   the timed netlist). FSM: IDLE -> (cycle 0 latch raw a/b/op into registers; do NOT
   negate here so the forwarding path is not lengthened) -> PREP (1 cycle: compute
   |a|, |b| from the registered raw values, clear remainder, record result signs)
   -> RUN (32 cycles of restoring shift/subtract: rem = {rem[30:0], q[31]};
   if rem >= div then rem -= div, q = {q[30:0],1} else q = {q[30:0],0}; one
   33-bit subtract + mux per cycle) -> FIX (1 cycle: conditional negate of quotient
   or remainder. RV32M corner cases: the plain restoring algorithm on magnitudes
   already yields q=all-ones and r=|a| for b==0, and q=0x80000000 / r=0 for
   INT_MIN/-1 after the normal sign fix-up, so the only explicit special case is
   DIV (signed) by 0, where the quotient sign fix-up must be bypassed so the result
   is all-ones rather than negated) ->
   DONE (result valid, busy=0; return to IDLE when the instruction advances out of
   EX, i.e. !stall_ex_mem). The latched operands make the result immune to the
   forwarding selects changing while EX is parked (the producer retires while the
   DIV waits, so fwd_sel falls to 0 and the stale ID/EX regfile value would be wrong).
   Wrap the whole FSM body in `ifndef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` -> under ALTOPS
   `busy = 0`, `done = 0` and the ALU's existing ALTOPS (a-b)^const stand-ins stay
   in force, so riscv-formal sees exactly the same single-cycle behaviour as today.

2. rtl/alu.sv: in the non-ALTOPS branch remove the four `/` `%` expressions (DIV
   ops fall through to `default: out = 0`; ex_stage substitutes the divider result).
   Keep the ALTOPS branch bit-identical. Replace the three multipliers by ONE
   signed 33x33 multiply: `a_ext = {a_signed & a[31], a}`, `b_ext = {b_signed & b[31], b}`
   with a_signed = (op==MULH || op==MULHSU) and b_signed = (op==MULH); take
   prod[31:0] for MUL and prod[63:32] for MULH/MULHU/MULHSU. This cuts DSP/LUT area
   and the output mux fan-in on the longest remaining path.

3. rtl/ex_stage.sv: decode `div_op = in.valid && alu_op in {DIV,DIVU,REM,REMU}`;
   instantiate `divider`; export `div_busy = div_op && !div_done` to the hazard unit
   (via core.sv). Result mux: `ex_result = div_op ? div_result : alu_result`
   (jump PC+4 override stays as is). EX/MEM register update: if (stall) hold; else if
   (div_busy) load a bubble (`reg_q <= '0`: valid=0, ctrl=0 so reg_write/mem ops are
   off and no forwarding from the bubble); else normal capture. For the DIV
   instruction's own capture in the DONE cycle, take `rs1_val`/`rs2_val`
   (RVFI-only fields) from the divider's latched a_q/b_q rather than the
   current forwarding muxes, so rvfi_rs1_rdata/rs2_rdata match the Python ISS in
   cosim; write_data/alu_result use the divider result. Under ALTOPS none of this
   is active (done/busy tied to 0, div_op path inert).

4. rtl/hazard_unit.sv + rtl/core.sv: new input `div_busy`. `stall_if` and `stall_id`
   gain `|| div_busy` (PC holds, ID/EX holds, IF/ID is a pure function of the held
   PC so nothing is lost); `flush_id = (load_use || redirect) && !dmem_stall && !div_busy`.
   `stall_ex_mem` and `hold_mem_wb` are unchanged: when the divider is busy the
   EX/MEM register takes a bubble and the older instruction in EX/MEM flows to
   MEM/WB normally. Once the bubble sits in EX/MEM, dmem_stall can no longer
   assert (no mem op in EX/MEM), so the only dmem/div overlap is the start cycle,
   which `start` explicitly guards with !stall_ex_mem (if the older mem op is still
   waiting on the bus, the DIV simply waits in IDLE, busy=1, EX/MEM held).
   redirect cannot fire while a DIV is in EX, so the IF redirect-priority logic is
   untouched.

5. Tests: test/test_alu.py keeps its non-DIV vectors (the ALU no longer produces
   DIV/REM in non-ALTOPS builds); move the existing DIV/REM vector set
   (by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, signed/unsigned, back-to-back) into a new
   test/test_divider.py that clocks the divider and waits for `done`, and add a
   pipeline test (test_pipeline.py) with DIV followed by a dependent ADD and a
   load-then-DIV so forwarding-before-latch and the dmem-stall start guard are
   covered. Invariant 5b (M-ext correctness) is thereby still covered by cocotb +
   cosim, and ALTOPS formal keeps proving bypass/stall behaviour unchanged.

Risks: (a) the first-cycle forwarding correctness (mitigated by latching at the
first non-dmem-stalled cycle, which is exactly the cycle baseline would have
committed that operand); (b) the new `busy` signal fans out to PC / ID/EX / EX/MEM
enables - it is derived from the ID/EX alu_op bits and a 2-bit FSM state, so it is
a 2-3 LUT path, far below the multiplier path; (c) if CoreMark's timed region
contains more divisions than expected, ~34 cycles each are charged to cycles, but
even 1000 divides would be <1% of the 4.49M-cycle run.

lesson: - 2026-10-01 hyp-20261001-001-r1s0 (improvement, +768.07%): Combinational `/` and `%` in alu.sv synthesized to a ~150-level array that capped Fmax at ~5 MHz, so moving DIV/REM into a multi-cycle serial divider (stall in EX via div_busy, bubble into EX/MEM) gave ~8.7x fitness because CoreMark's timed region barely divides; when the reported critical path is dozens of logic levels deep, look for rarely-executed ops to make iterative before touching IPC-side features.

title: Move MUL/DIV/REM out of the combinational ALU into a multi-cycle EX-stall muldiv unit
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.44 MHz (worst path 199.8 ns, 156 logic cells, 150 logic
levels): the critical path runs forwarding select -> EX operand mux ->
u_alu -> dmem address, and it is dominated by the purely combinational
32-bit `/` and `%` (signed + unsigned) plus three 32x32 multipliers that
alu.sv instantiates and muxes into the single-cycle ALU result. Every other
path in this 5-stage core (fwd mux -> 32-bit add -> EX/MEM / BSRAM address,
fwd -> 32-bit branch compare -> redirect -> PC) is only ~10-14 LUT levels,
i.e. roughly 20-30 ns. Fitness = iter/cycle x Fmax, and CoreMark executes
almost no divides inside the timed region and only ~0.4-1% multiplies (the
9x9 matrix kernels), so the single-cycle M-extension buys essentially no
IPC while costing ~7x in clock period and ~6-8k LUT4 of area.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Make M-extension ops multi-cycle and remove them from the combinational
ALU. Concretely:

1. New rtl/muldiv.sv with a clock/reset/start/op/a/b -> done/result
   interface. It latches the (post-forward) operands, then:
     - MUL/MULH/MULHU/MULHSU: ONE shared signed 33x33 multiplier (operands
       sign- or zero-extended to 33 bits per op) built as explicit
       16/17-bit partial products (maps to Gowin 18x18 DSPs) with a register
       after the partial products and a register after the 64-bit sum, so
       no path contains more than one DSP or one wide adder. Result mux
       picks [31:0] or [63:32]. 2-3 extra EX cycles per multiply (use the
       fewest stages that `make timing` shows are not critical).
     - DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU: iterative restoring divider, 1 bit/cycle (~34-36
       cycles): PREP (take absolute values, record signs), 32 shift/compare/
       subtract iterations on registered rem/quo/divisor, FIX (negate
       quotient if signs differ and divisor != 0, negate remainder if
       dividend negative). Divide-by-zero: quotient = all ones, remainder =
       dividend (suppress the quotient negate when b==0). INT_MIN/-1 falls
       out naturally (|INT_MIN|/1 with same signs -> 0x80000000, rem 0).
       All divider state is register-to-register, so none of it touches the
       forwarding/ALU critical path.

2. EX-stage stall handling (ex_stage.sv + hazard_unit.sv + core.sv).
   is_md_op = in.ctrl.alu_op >= ALU_MUL (decoder only emits >= 11 for legal
   M ops; bubbles/NOPs decode to ADD). md_busy = is_md_op && !md_done.
     - While md_busy: stall_if = 1 and stall_id = 1 (hold PC and ID/EX, flush_id
       stays 0 -- an M-op in EX is neither a load nor a redirect, so
       load_use and redirect are both 0), and the EX/MEM register captures a
       bubble (reg_q <= '0 => valid=0, reg_write=0, no mem op) UNLESS
       stall_ex_mem (dmem stall) is asserted, in which case EX/MEM simply
       holds (existing behaviour wins).
     - Operand capture: while the muldiv unit is IDLE it samples the
       forwarded rs1/rs2 every cycle; it only leaves IDLE on the first
       cycle where is_md_op && !stall_ex_mem. After that the forwarding
       muxes see bubbles / retired producers, so ONLY the latched operands
       may be used. In the final (DONE) cycle, EX/MEM.rs1_val / rs2_val
       (RVFI rs1_rdata / rs2_rdata, checked by cosim and riscv-formal) must
       come from the latched operands, and EX/MEM.alu_result <= md_result.
     - Leave condition: M-op leaves EX in the DONE cycle when
       !stall_ex_mem; the unit returns to IDLE the following cycle. If a
       dmem stall coincides with DONE, stay in DONE (result held).
     - Dependent consumers need no extra stall: the M-op's result is in
       EX/MEM.alu_result like any ALU op and is forwarded normally.

3. ALTOPS / formal: keep the `ifdef RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS branch exactly as
   today (combinational XOR-of-add/sub stand-ins in alu.sv) and under
   ALTOPS force is_md_op = 0 so the formal build never stalls; the real
   branch of alu.sv drops the mul/div expressions (default -> 0, M-op
   result comes from muldiv). This preserves invariant 5b: the real
   arithmetic is covered by cosim + a new cocotb test_muldiv.py (>=30
   vectors per M op incl. div-by-zero, INT_MIN/-1, signed corner cases)
   because test_alu.py's combinational M-ext vectors no longer apply to
   alu.sv and must be removed from it.

Expected effect: the 150-level ALU path disappears; the new critical path
is the ordinary forward -> add/compare -> redirect/EX-MEM/BSRAM-address
path (~20-30 ns), so Fmax should rise from ~5.4 MHz to roughly 30-45 MHz.
Cycle count rises by only ~1-3% (a few thousand multiplies x 2-3 stall
cycles out of ~449k cycles/iteration; divides are not in the timed loop in
any quantity), and LUT4 drops substantially because the combinational
divider and 2 of 3 wide multipliers vanish. Net fitness gain several x,
well beyond the 4.6% acceptance threshold (schema caps the reported delta
at +50).

title: Fetch-stage predecode predictor: JAL always-taken + 256-entry bimodal branches, EX-verified
motivation:
Every taken branch and every JAL/JALR currently resolves in EX and costs one
bubble (the wrong-path instruction sitting in IF/ID is killed and the PC is
redirected a cycle late). I traced the CoreMark binary on the reference ISS
(test/cosim/reference.py): 2,937,037 retired instructions, of which 532k are
conditional branches (296k taken), 49.6k JAL and 13.8k JALR, i.e. 0.122
taken redirects per instruction. Against the measured ~1.53 CPI
(4,491,485 cycles for 10 iterations) those bubbles are ~8% of all cycles.
The baseline critical path (199 ns, the combinational multiply/divide ALU
through fwd_unit/ex_stage, Fmax 5.44 MHz) leaves ~180 ns of slack on every
fetch/branch path, so a fetch-side predictor is free in Fmax terms: the only
thing it can change is cycles per iteration. A misprediction costs exactly
what a taken branch costs today (1 bubble), so the scheme only removes
cycles; it cannot regress IPC except for predicted-taken/actually-not-taken
branches, which I included in the estimate below.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a predictor in if_stage that exploits the fact that IF and ID are
merged (imem_data arrives in the same cycle as imem_addr = pc), so the
fetched word can be predecoded and the next PC chosen in that cycle, with
no BTB, no tags and no aliasing of targets:
  * JAL (opcode 1101111): always predicted taken, target = pc + J-imm
    (one 32-bit adder in IF, fed from imem_data).
  * Conditional branch (opcode 1100011): direction = MSB of a 2-bit
    saturating counter from a 256-entry bimodal table indexed by pc[9:2];
    target = pc + B-imm. Only predict taken if target[1:0] == 0 (keeps
    imem_addr aligned for symbolic misaligned-branch streams). The table is
    a plain array (no reset needed for correctness; any initial contents
    are verified away by EX, and an un-reset array maps to LUT-RAM), written
    only from EX when a valid conditional branch leaves EX
    (in.valid && is_branch && !stall_ex_mem, so a dmem-stalled branch
    trains once) with the actual taken bit.
  * JALR and everything else: predicted not-taken (pc+4), unchanged.
next_pc in if_stage becomes pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4. `redirect`
still has priority over everything and `stall` still holds the PC, so the
existing hazard_unit wiring is unchanged; pred_taken is only consumed when
the IF slot holds a real instruction (not stalled/flushed) and is zeroed in
the bundle for flushed/NOP slots. if_id_t and id_ex_t (core_pkg.sv) carry
pred_taken and pred_target; id_stage latches them (zero on reset/flush).
In ex_stage the resolved next PC (the expression already used for
reg_q.pc_next: misalign ? pc+4 : jump ? jump_target : taken ?
branch_target : pc+4) is compared with the predicted next PC
(pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4); redirect = in.valid && mismatch and
redirect_target = the resolved next PC. This verification makes aliasing,
JALR, misaligned-target and any non-branch cases safe, and RVFI
pc_wdata/pc_rdata continuity plus the misalign-trap behaviour stay
identical to the baseline because pc_next is still computed from the
resolved outcome, never from the prediction. A mispredict squashes the one
wrong-path instruction in IF/ID exactly as today. Offline replay of the
2.94M-instruction CoreMark control-flow trace gives: JAL 100% correct,
conditional-branch bimodal-256 ~87% accurate, net 0.102 redirect bubbles
removed per instruction (account for predicted-taken/actually-not-taken
costs) = ~84% of all baseline redirects, i.e. ~6.7% fewer cycles
(~7% more iterations/cycle). Discounting ~7% of that for redirects that
overlap a dmem stall today, I expect ~+6% fitness with Fmax unchanged,
because the new IF adder/mux and EX 32-bit compare are tens of ns against
the ~199 ns ALU path that sets Fmax. (Replay also shows a 4-entry RAS adds
only ~0.3% and gshare adds <0.3%, so both are left out to keep the change
small and low-risk.)

changes.description: Add pred_taken (1b) and pred_target (32b) to if_id_t and id_ex_t (zero in bubbles/flushed slots).

Predecode imem_data (JAL / BRANCH); add 256x2b bimodal counter array indexed by pc[9:2] with a write port driven from EX, the pc+J/B-imm adder, and next_pc = pred_taken ? pred_target : pc+4; drive pred_taken/pred_target on the IF/ID bundle (zero when flush/redirect/imem stall).
Latch pred_taken/pred_target into the ID/EX register (zero on reset/flush).

Compute the resolved next PC once; redirect = in.valid && (resolved_npc != predicted_npc), redirect_target = resolved_npc; emit a train strobe (pc[9:2], taken) gated by in.valid && is_branch && !stall.
Wire the EX train outputs back to if_stage; no top-level IO change.
Add pred_taken (1b) and pred_target (32b) to if_id_t and id_ex_t (zero in bubbles/flushed slots).

Latch pred_taken/pred_target into the ID/EX register (zero on reset/flush).
